narrative.overview: WoKim is a private developer workspace where projects appear as connected worlds rather than rows in a notebook. Deep indigo space, luminous paths, evidence planes, and compact human nodes make context visible, while standard navigation and forms keep daily operation immediate. The interface is calm but energized: cinematic at the first viewport, structured and legible in working screens, and never dependent on color alone for meaning.
keyCharacteristics: Dimensional midnight navigation with a bright, connected content field.
Manrope display type paired with workmanlike IBM Plex Sans body copy.
Cobalt-to-violet actions, cyan information signals, and coral attention markers.
Real evidence and generated product artwork instead of generic decoration.
A single current thread remains visible across the workspace.

rules.name: The Luminous Minority Rule
rules.body: Bright hues identify activity and connection; most working surface area remains neutral and readable.

rules.name: The Two-Speed Type Rule
rules.body: Display type creates entry-point emotion; body type returns immediately to efficient reading.

rules.name: The Three-Layer Rule
rules.body: A screen may combine ground, work surface, and one elevated focus layer; further shadow stacking is noise.

dos: Do give every major screen one clear visual anchor before dense work content begins.
Do use Lucide icons with labels for navigation and consequential actions.
Do preserve real screenshots, captions, OCR text, and source relationships as first-class visual evidence.
Do keep responsive behavior functional down to 320px and respect reduced-motion preferences.
donts: Don't return to uninterrupted white rows, thin rules, and table-first layouts as the dominant experience.
Don't fill pages with equal generic cards; vary hierarchy according to work state and importance.
Don't use gradients, orbit geometry, or 3D art without a work-memory meaning.
Don't hide state behind color, icon-only actions, or hover-only information.
